nodes.description: C-terminal truncating CPLX1 variants are predicted to impair complexin-1 function. Complete protein absence, nonsense-mediated decay and the effects of the reported missense alleles have not been demonstrated in patient material. Complexin binds SNAREs, while C-terminal membrane interactions are supported by nonhuman recombinant and worm studies. Loss of SNARE binding itself is not established for the patient C-terminal alleles.

nodes.description: Cplx1 knockout mice show early ataxia, selective thalamic and cerebellar volume loss, molecular-layer atrophy and loss of granule cells in selected cerebellar lobules. The structural phenotype was nonprogressive across the sampled ages. Neuronal loss was not detected in the molecular layer. These anatomical findings are not uniform human disease features.

evidence.reference_title: Tensor-based morphometry and stereology reveal brain pathology in the complexin1 knockout mouse.
evidence.snippet: Finally, stereology was used to show that there was loss of cerebellar granule cells in Cplx1(-/-) mice when compared to Cplx1(+/+) animals.

evidence.reference_title: Tensor-based morphometry and stereology reveal brain pathology in the complexin1 knockout mouse.
evidence.snippet: This suggests that, as with the behavioural phenotype, the pathological phenotype is non-progressive.

nodes.description: Acute brainstem slices reveal developmentally worsening loss of evoked and resting spontaneous transmission, but excessive poststimulus asynchronous release. Calcium influx, readily releasable pool size and quantal size were preserved. Elevated extracellular calcium rescued aspects of evoked release experimentally but is not a tested human therapy.

evidence.snippet: We therefore studied consequences of genetic ablation of Cplx1 in the mouse calyx of Held synapse, and discovered a developmentally exacerbating phenotype of reduced spontaneous and evoked transmission but excessive asynchronous release after stimulation, compatible with combined facilitating and clamping functions of Cplx1.

nodes.description: Evoked synaptic release is reduced after dual complexin-1/2 knockdown in cultured cortical neurons and after single Cplx1 knockout at mature mouse calyces of Held. These are experimental findings, not measurements in affected children.
